priceSnapshot.note: THE $64,500 CAP BROKE, AND IT BROKE ON SHORTS BEING FORCED OUT. Midnight handed over at $64,043 with a small spot add, a bullish tilt and one explicit trigger: a 4H close above $64,500. In the four hours since, BTC went 63,991 -> 64,867.2 in a near-straight line and the 08:00Z 4H candle is closing at $64,808 - the trigger has fired. The mechanism is verifiable rather than narrative: OKX's filled-liquidation feed shows 128 fills between 11:21Z and 12:03Z totalling roughly $797K, and every single one is a SHORT being bought back. Zero long liquidations in the window. Open interest is $2.005B, up 3.2% from midnight's $1.942B, so size is being added into the move rather than withdrawn, and the long/short ACCOUNT ratio has FALLEN from 1.58 to 1.40 while price rose $780 - accounts got less long into strength, which is the opposite of a crowded-long top. Equities agree: QQQ is bid $671.13 in pre-market, +1.42% on the Jul 29 close, after Microsoft's ~8% pop and its capex guide cut. The reason confidence is 5.75 and not higher: Q2 advance GDP, jobless claims and June core PCE all land at 08:30 ET, roughly 30 minutes after this snapshot, with consensus at 3.3% core and 3.7% headline. Price is also only at the TOP of the same range it has held all week - the Jul 24-26 highs sit at $65,373 and $65,727 - and the 15m RSI is 75.8. This is a real breakout arriving 30 minutes before a binary event.

It has never fired: the lowest print since the handover is $63,950.1 and the completed 4H closes are 63,999.3 and (closing now) 64,808.5. Separately, and tighter, the BREAKOUT fails if a 4H closes back under $64,150 - that is the 4H EMA20 ($64,217) and the $64,250-$64,500 base the move launched from. A close back inside that base does not trigger the structural reduce, it just cancels the long setup.

addIf.confirmation: A retest of the $64,250-$64,450 breakout base that HOLDS on a 1H close is where the cash recycled by this session's partial sale goes back to work. That band is the verified $88K liquidation shelf and the 15m EMA50 ($64,297) sits inside it. The larger momentum tranche is higher and separate: a 4H close above $65,000 opens the thin air toward $65,373 and $65,727, because nothing in the verified book rests between $65,000 and the range high.

What changed since 02:30 COT: (1) midnight's add trigger FIRED - the $64,500 cap and the 4H EMA50 ($64,436) are both cleared and price is now above every 15m, 1h and 4h EMA except the 1h EMA200 ($64,730 - also cleared, at 64,821) and above the DAILY EMA20 ($64,339) for the first time in the sequence; (2) the fuel is measured short liquidations, $797K in 42 minutes with zero longs, so this is forced buying rather than fresh conviction; (3) midnight's central worry inverted - it flagged the 1.58 long/short account ratio as crowded longs vulnerable to a downside sweep, and instead the ratio fell to 1.40 as price rose. Why take profit anyway: the wallet is 98% spot with 4 USDT of cash, so it has no ability to buy a retest; the squeeze clusters up to $64,861 have already been consumed; 15m RSI is 75.8; and core PCE prints in 30 minutes. Selling a small slice into forced buying to fund a retest bid is the trade. Probabilities move to bull 34 / range 44 / bear 22.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC, 30 sessions through the in-progress 2026-07-30 candle, seeded on the 2026-06-30 close of 58,620.3. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), Wilder-smoothed over 14. At 2.45% of spot a normal day covers about $1,589 - the entire $63,950-$64,867 move so far today is 58% of one average range, so the breakout is real but not yet extended by ATR standards.

The $63,000 reduce rail is carried into a sixth consecutive session and has still never fired; the lowest print since it was first set is $62,684 and the lowest since the last handover is $63,950.1.
calibration.note: Midnight gets a clean mark on both counts. Its ANALYSIS: it flipped the tilt to bullish on three specific grounds - the ETF outflow streak breaking at +$32.1M, Microsoft's capex cut removing the loudest equity bear argument, and the 4H MACD histogram crossing positive - and all three carried. Its ACTION: the 9 USDT spot add at $64,043 is up about 1.2% four and a half hours later, and the $64,500 add trigger it named fired almost exactly. Its one MISREAD is instructive rather than costly: it treated the 1.58 long/short account ratio as crowded longs and forecast 'a wick into $63,500-$63,700 before any real upside break as the higher-probability path'. The opposite happened - the ratio fell to 1.40 while price rose $780, meaning accounts were adding SHORTS into the move, and those shorts became the $797K of forced buying that produced the breakout. The sizing discipline that came with the wrong forecast (small add, powder reserved) cost nothing, so the correct lesson is about how to read a crowding snapshot, not about position size.
